metadata.title: Systematic review of research on artificial intelligence in K-12 education (2017–2022)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a systematic review of empirical studies on AI in K-12 education (2017–May 2022) and does not analyze any single ILSA micro-dataset. Therefore, there is no student-level sampling frame, no plausible-value (PV) scaling, and no application of complex survey weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) within this review. The review’s “sample” consists of included publications identified via PRISMA screening (66 included studies), not a representative student sample from an assessment program. Weighting guidance for ILSA PVs is not applicable here because the authors do not estimate achievement scores from ILSA microdata.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this is a systematic review that synthesizes findings across prior empirical studies rather than estimating PV-based achievement outcomes from ILSA microdata. The review does not report an analysis dataset with missing-item patterns or an imputation/deletion protocol for student-level variables. As a result, missing-data handling is not reported in the sense required for an empirical ILSA analysis.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The review included peer-reviewed journal articles or conference proceedings focused on AI in K-12 education, published from 2017 through May 2022, and excluded theoretical/conceptual pieces and review pieces. Screening proceeded in stages: initial title/abstract screening (276 deduplicated records → 137 retained), full-text retrieval (133 accessible), and full-text eligibility assessment (66 included). Exclusions at full-text level included non-English articles, non-K-12 settings, non-empirical studies, and non-peer-reviewed items.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Literature synthesis outcome (not student-level prediction), finding that This systematic review (PRISMA-guided) synthesizes 66 peer-reviewed studies on AI in K-12 education published between 2017 and May 2022. It does not conduct a new student-level predictive modeling analysis on any single ILSA dataset; instead, it reports descriptive synthesis of publication trends, research methodologies, AI themes, data collection methods, and AI techniques used across included studies. The review finds that publication volume increased after 2018, with the United States and China leading by number of included studies, and that qualitative methods were most common among the reviewed studies. Across the synthesized literature, supervised learning dominated, while unsupervised and reinforcement learning were comparatively rare. Reported performance metrics (e.g., accuracies) appear only within the included studies’ examples rather than being re-estimated or meta-analyzed here, and the review does not provide ILSA-specific PV handling, missing-data procedures, or survey-weighted estimation. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a systematic review rather than an empirical ILSA/NAEP-style analysis. Consequently, there is no assessment program/cycle/grade/domain, no student-level analytic sample, no PV-based achievement outcome, and no ML training/evaluation pipeline implemented by the authors on ILSA microdata. The main findings are therefore necessarily empty under the schema’s requirement for structured ML prediction results tied to a specific dataset and target variable.
